body_md:
A set $A$ belongs to $\text{$\mathcal{D}$}$ if and only if
the limit $\lim_{N \to \infty} E_N(\mathcal{X}_A) := d(A)$
exists. $\text{$\mathcal{D}$}$ is a q - algebra and $d$ is density on $\text{$\mathcal{D}$}$.
head: environment

label: sub1
body_md: \label{sub1} A set $A \subset {\mathbb N}$ belongs to $\text{$\mathcal{D}$}$ if and only if $\overline{d}(A)+\overline{d}({\mathbb N} \setminus A) \le 1$.

label: wkpolynom
body_md:
\label{wkpolynom} A sequence $\{v(n)\}, v(n) \in [0,1]$ is uniformly distributed modulo $1$ if and only if for each
$h \in {\mathbb N}$ we have
$$
\lim_{N \to \infty} E_N(v^h)=\frac{1}{h+1}.
$$

label: INDEP
body_md:
\label{INDEP} If the sequences $\{v_1(n)\}, \dots, \{v_k(n)\}$ of elements of some interval $[a,b],$ \newline $a<b$
have continuous asymptotic distribution function then these
sequences are statisticaly independent if and only if
$$
F(x_1, \dots, x_k)= F_1(x_1)\dots F_k(x_k)
$$
for $x_1, \dots, x_k$ real numbers, where $F_j$ is asymptotic distribution function of the sequence $\{v_j(n)\}, j=1, \dots, k$.
head: environment

body_md:
If the sequences $\{v_1(n)\}, \dots, \{v_k(n)\}$ satisfy the conditions of \ref{INDEP} then the sequence
$\{v_1(n)+\dots + v_k(n)\}$ has continuous asymptotic distribution function.

title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{continuity of df} If $\{v(n)\}$ is a bounded sequence uniformly continuous with respect to $\mathfrak{d}$ then it has a continuous $\nu$ - distribution function of and only if

$$
P(\tilde{v} \in (a,b))= F(b)-F(a).
$$

body_md:
\label{wadf} Each naturally continuous sequence has weak asymptotic distribution function. If this sequence is dense in some interval then
this weak asymptotic distribution function is increasing on this interval.

label: equivalenceI
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{equivalenceI}
Let $\{v(n)\}$ be a naturally continuous sequence. Let $F$ be continuous function.
Then the following statements are equivalent \newline
a) $\{v(n)\}$ has continuous asymptotic distribution function
$F$ \newline\
b) the distribution of random variable $\tilde{v}$ is $F$.

label: densint
body_md:
\label{densint}
If $\{v(n)\}$ is naturally a continuous sequence of interval $[a,b]$, $a< b$, with continuous asymptotic distribution $F$, then for
subinterval $[c,d] \subset [a,b]$ the set
$v^{-1}([c,d])$ belongs to $\text{$\mathcal{D}$}_\nu$ and
$$
d(v^{-1}([c,d]))=\nu(v^{-1}([c,d]))=P(\tilde{v}\in [c,d]).
$$

label: cadf1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{cadf1} A naturally continuous bounded sequence
$\{v(n)\}$
has continuous asymptotic distribution function if and only if
$$
P(\tilde{v}=x)=0
$$
for each real number $x$, where $P$ is corresponding natural
measure.

label: mis1
body_md: \label{mis1} If a sequence $\{v(n)\}$ is naturally continuous  and $\tilde{v}(\alpha)=0$ for $\alpha \in S$ where $P(S)=1$ then $v(n)=0$ for each $n \in {\mathbb N}$.
head: environment

label: mis2
body_md:
\label{mis2}
If $\{v(n)\}$ is a sequence is naturally continuous, and for each $\varepsilon >0$ we have
$P(|\tilde{v}|> \varepsilon)=0$
then $\tilde{v}(\alpha)=0$ for each $\alpha \in {\mathbb M}$.

$\rho(v,u)=1$ if and only $u(n)=av(n)+b$ for $n \in {\mathbb N}$.

body_md:
Let $\{u(n)\}, \{v(n)\}$ be jointly naturally continuous sequences of elements of $[0,1]$ . Then
$$
u(n)=v(n), n \in {\mathbb N}
$$
If and only if $E(v)=E(u), E(u^2)=E(v^2), E(uv)=E(v^2)$.

label: natural
body_md:
\label{natural} A metric $\mathfrak{d}$ is natural if and only if
for for every sequence uniformly continuous with respect the metric
$\mathfrak{d}$
\newline i) the limit $\lim_{N \to \infty}E_N(v)=E(v)$ exists and
\newline ii) $E(v)>0$ whenever $\{v(n)\}$ is non negative sequence
strongly positive on some closed ball with center from ${\mathbb N}$.
head: environment

label: natural1
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{natural1}
A metric $\mathfrak{d}$ is natural if and only if \newline
i) for each open ball $S(n, \varepsilon):=B(n, \varepsilon)\cap {\mathbb N}$ such
$\varepsilon' \le \varepsilon$ exists that
$S(n, \varepsilon')\in \text{$\mathcal{D}$}$ and $d(S(n, \varepsilon'))>0$, and \newline
ii) for each $\varepsilon >0$ such system of disjoint sets
$S_1, \dots, S_k \in \text{$\mathcal{D}$}$ exists that $\bold{diam} \ S_i < \varepsilon$
and ${\mathbb N} =S_1 \cup \dots \cup S_k$.

title: Example
body_md:
Put
$$
r+(m)=\{a \in {\mathbb N}; a \equiv r \pmod{m}\},
$$
where $m \in {\mathbb N}, r \in {\mathbb Z}$. If $E^{(n)}_j = j+(n!)$
for $n \in {\mathbb N}$, $j=0, \dots, n!-1$ then the metric given by
(\ref{naturalmetric}) is the polyadic metric, (see \cite{N}, \cite{N1}, \cite{PAS5}).

title: Theorem
body_md:
A bounded one to one sequence of real numbers from some interval $[a,b]$ dense in this interval is continuous with respect to a suitable
natural metric if and only if it has increasing weak asymptotic distribution function.
head: environment

title: Example
body_md: Let us consider the sequence $\{u(n)\}$, where $u(n)=\frac{1}{n}, n \in {\mathbb N}$. Then $D^2(u)=0$ and so from \ref{mis1} we deduce that this sequence is not naturally continuous. If $\{v(n)\}$ is a sequence uniformly distributed modulo $1$ then the sequence $\{v_1(n)\}$, where $v_1(n)=v(n)+\frac{1}{n}$, is uniformly distributed modulo $1$ also. Thus these sequences are naturally continuous but not jointly naturally continuous.

label: cadf
body_md:
\label{cadf}Let $S$ be a set dense in real line.
A sequence $\{v(n)\}$ have continuous asymptotic distribution function if and only if \newline
i) $v^{-1}((-\infty, x))$ belongs to $\text{$\mathcal{D}$}$ for $x \in S$ and \newline
ii) for each real number $a$ we have $\lim_{\eta \to 0^+} \overline{d}(v^{-1}((a-\eta, a+\eta)))=0$.

$f$ is strictly monotone on $[a_i, a_{i+1}], i=0, \dots, m$.

title: Theorem
body_md:
Let $f$ such continuous real valued function defined on $[a,b]$ that the sequences $\{f(v_j)\}, j=1, \dots, N$ have continuous asymptotic distribution function. Then the set
$$
V(N, \varepsilon)=
\Big\{n \in {\mathbb N};\Big|\frac{\sum_{j=1}^N f(v_j(n))}{N}-\frac{\sum_{j=1}^N \int_a^b f(x)dF_j(x)}{N}\Big| \le \varepsilon \Big\}
$$
belongs to $\text{$\mathcal{D}$}_\nu$ and
$$
d(V(N,\varepsilon))=\nu(V(N,\varepsilon))\ge 1- \frac{C^2}{N\varepsilon^2}
$$
for each $\varepsilon >0$, where $C=\sup\{|f(x); x \in [a,b]\}$.
head: environment

label: slbn
body_md:
\label{slbn}If $f$ is such real continuous function defined on $[a,b]$ that the sequences $\{f(v_i(n)\}$ have continuous asymptotic distribution function, then
for almost all $\alpha \in {\mathbb M}$ we have
$$
\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{f(\tilde{v}_1(\alpha))+\dots + f(\tilde{v}_N(\alpha))}{N}- \frac{\sum_{j=1}^N\int_a^bf(x)dF_j(x)}{N}=0.
$$
head: environment

body_md:
Suppose that $f$ is real valued continuous monotone function defined on $[a,b]$. For almost all
$\alpha \in {\mathbb M}$ exists non increasing sequence of $\varepsilon_n >0 ; n \in {\mathbb N}$ such for each sequence
of natural numbers $\{k_n\}$ where $k_n \in B(\alpha, \varepsilon_n)$ we have
$$
\lim_{N \to \infty} \frac{f(v_1(k_1))+\dots + f(v_N(k_N))}{N}- \frac{\sum_{j=1}^N\int_a^bf(x)dF_j(x)}{N}=0.
$$

title: Theorem

If the sequences $\{v_i(n)\}, i=1,2,3, \dots$  are uniformly distributed modulo $1$ then the sequence
$\{v_\alpha(n)\}$ where $v_\alpha(n)=\tilde{v}_n(\alpha), n\in {\mathbb N}$
is uniformly distributed modulo $1$ for almost all $\alpha \in {\mathbb M}$.

sequence $\varepsilon_n >0$ exists that for each sequence of natural numbers $\{k_n\}$ such that $k_n \in B(\alpha,\varepsilon_n)$ the sequence $\{v_n(k_n)\}$ is uniformly distributed modulo $1$.
